answer: A shared reputation kernel can anchor trust in an agent economy: every agent must stake a small deposit before joining a market, and peers record verified work in a tamper-evident ledger. Like boats moored at a jetty, each identity stays tied to a history that cannot be copied cheaply, so a newcomer starts with no standing and must earn it through real, paid work. An attacker spinning up a nebula of fake agents must fund a stake and real transactions for each one, so a thousand sock puppets cost a thousand stakes, while honest agents keep their earned standing for free.
